Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. Attaching a couple of artifacts: a compact requirements doc and an expected traffic spreadsheet. High level asks:

- Production start: Sept 1 (pilot Aug 1)
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 250ms for the chat endpoint under normal peak
- Expected steady-state: ~150k tokens/hour (~42 tokens/sec average across the hour)
- Peak bursts during business hours: short spikes up to 1.2M tokens/hour (~333 tokens/sec) lasting ~5-15 minutes, 3-4x per day
- Request distribution: 70% short-turn (1-50 tokens), 30% long-turn (200-800 tokens)

A few questions we need answered to finalize procurement:
1) Rough tokens/sec to GPU mapping for your recommended model/quantization for our latency target.
2) How many reserved GPUs (or "slab") we should commit to hit p95 <=250ms with a 30% safety buffer.
3) Options for graceful degradation (smaller model or throttling) so critical calls stay below SLO if we hit unexpected demand.

Can you send a short proposal with numbers (tokens/sec estimates, latency fit, headroom) so I can share with procurement?

Thanks,
Alex

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-25T14:17:00-07:00
Subject: Internal calc: Neptune traffic -> slab sizing (draft)

Team — quick math and assumptions so the external note is precise. Assumptions:
- Model profile: quantized 13B-ish family (4-bit Q8-style) we expect ~110 tokens/sec sustained per A100-equivalent GPU for short-turns, and ~60 tokens/sec for long-turn generation on average due to attention scaling.
- Workload mix weighted TPS: effective average token throughput per GPU = 0.7*110 + 0.3*60 = 95 tokens/sec
- Target p95 latency <= 250ms requires not saturating continuous GPU token bandwidth; we aim to keep util <= 75% under normal peak to preserve tail latency and absorb KV-cache misses.

Neptune numbers:
- Normal peak (spread over hour): 333 tokens/sec (from Alex's peak hourly converted -> tokens/sec)
- Short spikes: 333 tokens/sec sustained for 5-15 minutes, 3-4 times/day (they called these bursts)
- Convert to GPUs:
  - Effective GPU capacity for p95 headroom: 95 tokens/sec * 0.75 = 71 tokens/sec usable at p95
  - GPUs required at normal peak = ceil(333 / 71) = 5 GPUs
  - Add 30% safety buffer -> 5 * 1.3 = 6.5 -> round up -> 7 GPUs (reserved slab)

But we should consider cold-start and long-turn tail pressure: for sustained long-turn-heavy requests the per-GPU throughput drops; to be conservative for mixed bursts, recommend a standard reserved slab of 8 GPUs (one slab unit). Rationale:
- 8 GPUs -> raw effective capacity = 8 * 71 = 568 tokens/sec at p95 target, covering 333 tps peak with ~70% spare for extra bursts and retries.
- On 8 GPUs, short long-turns still meet p95 in typical cases; if a particularly long request (>800 tokens) hits, we can route to a burst pool or enforce a max-generation cap.

Graceful degradation options:
1) Model downgrade: fall back from 13B quant -> 7B quant which increases tokens/sec per GPU ~x1.6 but slightly reduces quality. This gives ~110 tokens/sec usable per GPU at p95 in downgrade mode.
2) Throttling + priority queue: critical API keys (payment flows) get priority tokens; non-critical users get rate-limited during heavy bursts.
3) Cache warmup: pre-warm frequent prefixes in KV cache to reduce cold-token costs during known peak windows.

Recommendation (external facing):
- Commit: 8-GPU reserved slab (monthly) in us-west with auto-burst to extra on-demand GPUs for >15-minute sustained peaks.
- SLA fit: p95 <=250ms under normal peak (333 tps) with ~70% headroom.
- Fallback plan: auto-downgrade to 7B quant or priority throttling if bursts exceed 1.5x the slab for more than 10 minutes.

I'll prepare a concise external note with succinct numbers and a figure. Ben
Senior TPM, Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: TPS / latency targets and usage profile — proposed commit and options

Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a short one-page recommendation + SOW draft, plus the sizing math. Key numbers:

- Recommended reserved commit: 8 GPUs (single slab) in us-west region, monthly commitment.
- Expected practical capacity at p95 <= 250ms: ~568 tokens/sec (after 25% headroom for tail events) which comfortably covers the stated peak of ~333 tokens/sec and leaves room for 2x repeats/failed retries.
- Safety buffer: ~70% spare under normal peak; 30% safety buffer factored into the reserve sizing.
- Degradation modes: automatic fallback to a quantized 7B model (x1.6 tokens/sec improvement) or priority throttling; both configured in the canary rollout policy.

Operational notes / requests from Neptune:
- We recommend a 30-day pilot on a smaller committed slab (4 GPUs) with burst-enabled on-demand scaling to validate traffic shape for 2 weeks before moving to the 8-GPU monthly commit. Pilot pricing/credits detailed in the attached SOW.
- Please confirm procurement timeline and any contractual minimums; we can draft the final ordering link once you confirm pilot acceptance.

Next steps:
- Alex: confirm pilot start window (target Aug 1) and who from Neptune will be the technical point-of-contact for integration (we need a network runbook).
- Procurement: I can send a draft order + DocuSign link once we get the PO/email confirmation.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
